Subject: Non-standard SLA annex for batch inference: latency carve-outs & evidence

Hi Dana / Michael,

Thanks again for the time today — good to align on Orchard's high-throughput inference profile. As discussed, you have a subset of workflows that are batch-heavy (large batch scoring windows) where per-request tail latency isn't the primary business metric, and you'd like our standard availability/latency language to be adjusted so we can:

- Allow short, documented latency exceptions during scheduled batch windows
- Define clear acceptance criteria for throughput vs per-request p95/p99
- Agree an evidence package (telemetry, KV cache hits, rollout notes) that supports the exception

I attached a first-pass "proposed-sla-annex-v1.docx" and a draft ops runbook that describes how we plan to route batch jobs, fall back to a lower-cost model variant, and notify your oncall if capacity is impacted. Key asks from your side so we can convert this into order-form language:

1) Confirmation of the batch windows (local time) and expected peak RPS and average token lengths
2) Which telemetry classifiers your procurement/legal team needs as evidence (raw token-level latency traces vs aggregated tables)
3) Any minimum ramp / blackout windows for deploys during those batch runs

Proposed next steps:
- You review the annex and runbook; mark items that require legal redlines
- If acceptable, we produce a short order-form amendment with the annex attached for signature (DocuSign)

I'll loop in Neha (legal) and Marissa (CS) for order-form wording and evidence acceptance — cc'd.

Thanks,

Thanks Aisha — reviewed with our procurement and infra leads. A few quick clarifications before we escalate to legal: 

- For evidence, procurement wants aggregated telemetry (p50/p95/p99) plus a daily digest during the first 30 days of the pilot. Raw traces are fine for a *limited* scoped audit, but not as a recurring deliverable.
- Can you clarify the maximum duration and frequency of the "latency exception" windows? Our compliance team is worried about open-ended carve-outs.
- We need suggested fallback SLAs if Redwood falls back to a lower-cost model (e.g., model-variant X): what are the expected delta on latency and availability?

Also: happy to accept the annex in principle but legal will want clean order-form language we can attach to the MSA. Can Marissa / Neha propose concrete order-form wording rather than sending the full annex as a standalone doc?

Thanks,

Michael — great questions, thanks. Quick answers and a proposed path: 

- Evidence cadence: Redwood can deliver aggregated telemetry (p50/p95/p99, mean throughput, cache hit %) daily for the 30-day pilot and weekly thereafter. Raw traces we will provide on-demand for scoped audits (with an agreed retention window).
- Exception windows: propose we define them explicitly in the order form as "Scheduled Batch Window" entries (date/time ranges OR recurring cron-style windows). Each window can have a maximum duration per 24h (e.g., up to 4 hours) and a maximum frequency (e.g., 3 occurrences per week) — we can make these numbers configurable per customer.
- Fallback model deltas: Attached in the annex is a table of expected service deltas when we route to a lower-cost quantized model variant (avg token throughput + expected p95/p99 increases). For order-form simplicity, we can codify fallback tiers and their committed minimum availability; see the draft orderform-amendment-draft.docx I've attached for language suggestions.

Marissa / Neha — can you review the draft orderform wording in the attached docx and propose: 1) a concise clause to add to the order form that enumerates "Scheduled Batch Windows" and allowable exception rules, and 2) an acceptance/evidence definition (what aggregated artifacts satisfy the exception)? Procurement indicated they prefer a short paragraph in the order form + the annex as a referenced attachment rather than embedding all technical detail inline.

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-min redline call tomorrow with procurement and your legal rep to speed this up.

Best,

Hi Michael / Dana — looping in from legal. Thanks for the clear asks. Below is proposed, concise order-form language we can attach to the MSA and push to signature; the annex and ops runbook remain as referenced attachments. Please review and flag any hard stops.

PROPOSED ORDER-FORM CLAUSE (for insertion into the Customer Order Form)
"Scheduled Batch Window Exception. Notwithstanding the Service Availability commitments in the MSA, Customer and Redwood agree that during mutually agreed Scheduled Batch Windows (defined in the attached SLA Annex), Redwood may apply temporary latency tolerance thresholds to accommodate high-throughput batch scoring. Any Scheduled Batch Window must be documented in the Order Form by start/end times or recurring schedule. The total duration of Scheduled Batch Windows shall not exceed the limits set forth in the Order Form. During a Scheduled Batch Window Redwood will: (a) provide aggregated telemetry (p50/p95/p99, mean throughput, cache hit rate) at the cadence stated in the Order Form; (b) implement agreed fallback routing to alternate model variants if capacity constraints arise; and (c) notify Customer oncall per the notification procedure in the attached Ops Runbook. The application of this exception will not modify Redwood's availability credits structure except as expressly stated in the Order Form."

EVIDENCE ACCEPTANCE (summary)
- Pilot (first 30 days): daily aggregated telemetry (CSV) plus weekly summarized report; raw traces available on request for scoped audits
- Production: weekly aggregated telemetry and monthly summary unless otherwise agreed
- Retention: Redwood will retain telemetry artifacts for 90 days unless Customer requests extended retention in writing

ORDER-FORM FIELDS (suggested)
- Scheduled Batch Window(s): [start/end or cron]
- Max duration per day: [numeric hours]
- Max frequency per week: [numeric occurrences]
- Evidence cadence (pilot/production)
- Fallback tier mapping (variant name -> expected p95 delta)

Attachments sent to procurement/legal: orderform-amendment-draft.docx (suggested insertion), proposed-sla-annex-v1.docx, ops-runbook-draft.pdf.

Next steps I propose:
1) Michael/Dana confirm the concrete batch windows and the maximum duration/frequency you want in the order form
2) Aisha book an expedited redline session (30 mins) for Monday morning PT to get procurement and Orchard legal into the same doc
3) Upon agreement we’ll produce a DocuSign-ready order form amendment and route for signature (I can own legal side of redlines)

If that sounds good I’ll prepare a redline-ready copy of the order form clause and the short evidence checklist.

Regards,
